title: Chapter 2 Quiz
description: Test your mastery of Pods – anatomy, YAML, management, and lifecycle.

questions.question: What is a Pod in Kubernetes?
options: A grouping of one or more containers with shared storage/network
questions.explanation: A Pod is the smallest deployable unit that can contain multiple containers sharing namespaces.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT shared between containers in the same Pod?
questions.explanation: PID namespace sharing is optional; by default each container has its own PID namespace.

questions.question: The special container that holds the network namespace for a Pod is called the _____ container.
questions.explanation: The pause container anchors the network namespace and exists for the Pod's lifetime.

questions.question: True or False: Two containers in a Pod can bind to the same port if they use different protocols.
questions.explanation: The network stack is shared, so port numbers must be unique regardless of protocol.

questions.question: Which Kubernetes API version should you use for a Pod?
questions.explanation: Pods belong to the core API group, so apiVersion: v1.

questions.question: What is the purpose of labels in Kubernetes?
questions.explanation: Labels are key-value pairs used for grouping and selecting resources.

questions.question: Which command applies a YAML manifest to the cluster?
questions.explanation: kubectl apply -f is the declarative way to create or update resources.

questions.question: What does `kubectl get pods -o wide` show that `kubectl get pods` does not?
questions.explanation: -o wide adds columns for Node and IP address.

questions.question: How can you delete all Pods with the label 'app=test'?
options: Both b and c are correct
questions.explanation: -l and --selector are equivalent and accept label queries.

questions.question: Which kubectl command shows detailed events for a Pod?
questions.explanation: kubectl describe pod includes a section of recent events.

questions.question: To get an interactive shell inside a container, use kubectl exec _____ <pod-name> -- /bin/sh.
questions.explanation: -i (stdin) and -t (TTY) are needed for interactive sessions.

questions.question: Which pattern describes a helper container that proxies network traffic for the main container?
questions.explanation: Ambassador containers sit between the main app and the outside world.

questions.question: True or False: Init containers run after the main containers start.
questions.explanation: Init containers run to completion before any main container is started.

questions.question: What Pod phase indicates that all containers have terminated successfully?
questions.explanation: Succeeded means all containers exited with code 0.

questions.question: Which restartPolicy should you use for a batch job that must not restart on failure?
questions.explanation: Never ensures the Pod will not be restarted automatically.

questions.question: What does CrashLoopBackOff indicate?
options: The node is out of memory
questions.explanation: The kubelet backs off restarting a container that crashes quickly after starting.

questions.question: To see logs from a previous crashed container, use kubectl logs _____ <pod>.
questions.explanation: --previous retrieves logs from the terminated container instance.

questions.question: Which command forwards a local port to a Pod?
questions.explanation: kubectl port-forward pod/<name> local-port:pod-port creates a tunnel.

questions.question: True or False: A multi‑container Pod must have at least one volume defined.
questions.explanation: Volumes are optional; containers can communicate via localhost without any shared volume.

questions.question: Which field in a Pod spec is mandatory?
questions.explanation: At minimum, spec must contain a containers list.
